system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Spinner]

Roland’s spinner has three sectors of different colors, orange, purple, and green. Roland spins the pointer 1000 times. The chart below shows how many times the pointer stops on each section.

| Color | Times Stopped |
| :--- | :---: |
| Orange | 510 |
| Purple | 243 |
| Green | 247 |

Draw lines on the spinner above to make the three sectors the approximate size you would expect them to be. Label them orange, purple, and green.

Figure, described in words:
A circular spinner with a central circular hub and an arrow pointer angled upward and to the right. Around the circumference of the circle is an outer rim with 8 equally spaced tick marks, dividing the circle into 8 equal arcs of 45° each (at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30). The interior of the circle is blank.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Orange was stopped 510 out of 1000 times, about 51%, so the orange sector should take up about half the circle (about 180°, i.e., about 4 of the 8 equal arcs). Purple (243) and green (247) are each about 24–25%, so each should take up about a quarter of the circle (about 90°, i.e., about 2 of the 8 equal arcs). Draw one straight line from the center to the 12 o'clock tick mark and another from the center to the 6 o'clock tick mark, dividing the circle into two halves. Label the right half (from 12 o'clock clockwise to 6 o'clock) orange. Then draw a line from the center to the 9 o'clock tick mark to divide the left half into two quarters. Label the upper-left quarter (from 12 o'clock counterclockwise to 9 o'clock) purple, and the lower-left quarter (from 9 o'clock to 6 o'clock) green.
